body:
## Finding

`ServerConfig` is fully built and parsed — and nothing in production ever loads it. The config half of #798 landed in PR #1801 (merged 39e8410b, 2026-10-29): a `[policy]` table with `freshness_window_seconds` + `pull_policy`, `[budgets]`, typed accessors, and startup-failing parse errors. Since then the remainder of #798 (consumption by `id serve` / sync sessions) has stayed blocked, and a fresh check at main `3b8d3215d808` (2026-11-03T20:15Z, task 2657 resume) shows why: there is still no production consumption point to wire the config *into*. This issue is that missing integration work, split out of #798 so the block has a name.

## Evidence (fresh, main `3b8d3215d808`)

- `ServerConfig::load` (`pkgs/id/src/server_config/mod.rs:178`) has **no caller** outside `server_config`'s own tests (`parse.rs`). Code search for `server_config::` hits only `server_config/{mod,parse,provision}.rs` and a doc mention in `pull_policy.rs`.
- `id serve` (`pkgs/id/src/commands/serve.rs`, 3038 lines) has **no server-config flag and never references `server_config`**; its `resolve_config` is the unrelated CLI bootstrap/topic defaults.
- The only production `PullGate` construction is `event_sync::open_gate()` — hard-coded `PullPolicy::Open` over a `NoWorlds` membership stub — called at `serve.rs:1256` for the node's own event-store sync. `event_sync.rs` documents why: "there is no world whose membership this store belongs to." Every `PullPolicy::Members` gate in the tree is in tests (`log_sync.rs`, `event_store/sync.rs`, `pull_policy.rs`). `pull_policy.rs:22-23` still states it plainly: "`id serve` does not read it yet, and no session builds a gate from config."
- The freshness consumer does not exist in production either: `seitan::admit` (the only caller of the `Freshness` window) is referenced only by `seitan`'s own tests and a design spike under `doc/`. `Freshness` is constructed in production nowhere outside `server_config::freshness()` itself, which nothing calls.
- `Provisioned::apply` (startup provisioning from the same config) likewise has no production caller — the whole file is dead at runtime, not just the `[policy]` table.

## Scope

- `id serve` learns to load a server config (path flag in the existing CLI style; absent = today's behaviour, code defaults everywhere) and fails startup on a parse error, matching `ServerConfig::parse`'s contract.
- Serve builds its sync pull gate(s) from `config.pull_policy()`; where a gate's store has no world membership (the `event_sync` own-store case), the design must say what `members` means there — refuse-all, refuse-startup-with-a-clear-error, or a membership source — and not silently serve open.
- The invite-admission path that consumes `config.freshness()` is wired where seitan admission is actually served, or that consumer is built as part of this work.
- Startup provisioning (`Provisioned::apply`) runs from the loaded config.
- Once landed, #798's remainder closes: pull policy + freshness consumed from config, and `doc/2026-10-14T_platform_completion/acceptance-brief.md` line 76 checked off.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `id serve` with a config file naming `pull_policy = "members"` demonstrably refuses a non-member pull in a test, and with no config file behaves exactly as today
- [ ] A malformed config file fails `id serve` startup with the parse error named
- [ ] The configured freshness window reaches the seitan admission check that serve runs (test at the configured value, not the 5-minute default)
- [ ] #798's remaining acceptance items are verified against this change and #798 is closed or its remainder re-scoped

## Out of scope

- Changes to the `[policy]`/`[budgets]` parse surface itself (landed, PR #1801)
- Blob gating (`blob_gate` already requires membership independently)
